title: Create the repository and project README
acceptance: The GitHub repository is accessible to the student.
The English README describes the application and planned components.
Git ignores build output, credentials and local database files.
commit: docs: add project overview and development workflow
commit_steps: Add the English README.
Add Git ignore rules and editor settings.

title: Set up the GitHub Project and development tasks
acceptance: The Project has Todo, In progress and Done statuses.
At least 20 issues have labels, explicit due dates and acceptance criteria.
Issues are added to the Project and reference their planned task IDs.
commit: docs: add requirements checklist and issue backlog
commit_steps: Add the requirements checklist and development plan.
Record the issue list, due dates and GitHub workflow templates.

title: Create the solution and application scaffold
acceptance: The .NET solution contains API, shared contracts, Worker and test projects with clear responsibilities.
The React JavaScript frontend is separate from the API and uses it over HTTP.
The README gives tested commands for the API, React website and Worker on Windows with VS Code.
commit: chore: create application solution and project scaffold
commit_steps: Create the .NET solution and API, contracts, Worker and test projects.
Create the React JavaScript frontend.
Document and check the startup commands.

title: Define the budget entities and relationships
acceptance: The model has at least five related tables.
Transactions, budgets, rules and imports belong to a user.
Amounts use decimal values and transaction dates have a defined format.
commit: feat: define budget entities and relationships
commit_steps: Add users, categories and transaction models.
Add budget, category rule, import and report relationships.

title: Add EF Core migrations and seed data
acceptance: EF Core migrations create the PostgreSQL schema using a configured connection.
Synthetic categories and transactions can be seeded without duplicating existing seed records.
The setup can be repeated on a second computer without deleting existing shared data.
commit: feat: add EF Core migrations and seed data
commit_steps: Create the first PostgreSQL migration.
Add repeatable synthetic seed data and setup instructions.

title: Add repositories and register application services
acceptance: Repositories encapsulate data access needed by the application.
Business logic uses injected repositories and services.
Only API-side projects reference the database implementation.
commit: feat: add repositories and service registration
commit_steps: Add repository interfaces and implementations.
Register the services and dependencies in the API.

title: Add JWT login and User Admin Service roles
acceptance: Registration and login return suitable responses and passwords are hashed.
User, Admin and Service access restrictions are enforced.
JWT signing secrets and service passwords come from local configuration.
commit: feat: add JWT authentication and role policies
commit_steps: Implement registration, password hashing and login.
Add JWT validation and User, Admin and Service access rules.

title: Add DTO validation and consistent API errors
acceptance: Public endpoints accept and return DTOs rather than database entities.
Invalid requests produce clear validation errors.
Unexpected errors use global ProblemDetails handling and are logged without exposing secrets.
commit: feat: add API validation and ProblemDetails errors
commit_steps: Define request and response DTOs and input validation.
Add global ProblemDetails handling and logging.

title: Document API requests in Swagger and an HTTP file
acceptance: Swagger shows endpoint descriptions, request examples and JWT Authorize.
CORS permits the configured web-client origin.
An HTTP request file covers authentication and is extended as endpoints are added.
commit: feat: configure Swagger CORS and HTTP request examples
commit_steps: Configure Swagger descriptions, examples and Authorize.
Add CORS and an HTTP request file for the implemented endpoints.

title: Add transaction and category CRUD endpoints
acceptance: A user can create, read, edit and delete their transactions and categories.
Income and expenses have valid amounts, dates, descriptions and categories.
Another user's records cannot be read or changed and HTTP status codes are appropriate.
commit: feat: add transaction and category endpoints
commit_steps: Implement category endpoints and ownership checks.
Implement transaction CRUD and appropriate HTTP responses.

title: Add transaction search filters sorting and pagination
acceptance: GET /api/transactions supports from, to and category filters.
Text search, supported sorting and bounded pagination work together.
Empty results and invalid filter parameters have predictable responses.
commit: feat: add transaction search filters and pagination
commit_steps: Add search, date and category filters.
Add supported sorting and bounded pagination.

title: Calculate monthly income expenses and balance
acceptance: The summary is scoped to the signed-in user and selected month.
Income, expenses and balance match known example transactions.
A month with no transactions returns zero totals.
commit: feat: calculate monthly financial summaries
commit_steps: Implement the monthly total calculations.
Add the summary endpoint and calculation tests.

title: Build React login and registration screens
acceptance: The user can register, log in and log out through the API.
Protected pages handle missing or expired sessions.
Forms validate input and show useful API errors.
commit: feat: add web authentication screens
commit_steps: Build the React registration and login forms.
Add session handling, logout and protected routes.

title: Build React transaction management screens
acceptance: The site lists, adds, edits and deletes transactions using the API.
Search, filters, sorting and pagination are available in the UI.
Loading, empty and error states are understandable and forms validate input.
commit: feat: add web transaction management
commit_steps: Build the React transaction list and forms.
Connect search, filters, sorting and pagination to the API.

title: Add monthly budgets and the summary dashboard
acceptance: GET /api/budgets/{month}/summary returns the monthly totals and budget information.
The user can set and update a monthly budget.
The site shows remaining budget and a clear overspending warning.
commit: feat: add monthly budgets and dashboard
commit_steps: Add the budget settings and monthly summary API.
Build the React dashboard and overspending warning.

title: Add automatic category rules and their management screen
acceptance: CRUD /api/category-rules is scoped to the current user.
The UI can add, edit and delete rules such as Rimi to Food.
Case handling and precedence for multiple matching rules are documented and tested.
commit: feat: add automatic category rules
commit_steps: Implement rule CRUD and matching logic.
Add the React rule management screen and matching tests.

title: Accept CSV uploads and expose import status
acceptance: A documented CSV format and a synthetic sample file are supplied.
POST /api/imports validates an upload and returns 202 with an import ID.
GET /api/imports/{id} returns only the owner's import status and the UI can upload a file.
commit: feat: add CSV upload and import status
commit_steps: Add CSV upload validation and import status endpoints.
Add the upload screen and a synthetic sample file.

title: Process queued import rows through batch endpoints
acceptance: Service can list pending imports and process up to 100 rows per batch through the specified endpoints.
Processing applies category rules, records progress and reports invalid rows clearly.
Retrying a completed batch or resuming an import does not add the same stored rows twice.
commit: feat: add resumable batch import processing
commit_steps: Add pending-import and batch-processing endpoints.
Handle invalid rows and safe retries with relevant checks.

title: Connect the Worker to the import API
acceptance: A separate BackgroundService logs in with its Service account and uses HttpClient.
PeriodicTimer checks for pending imports every 10 seconds and processes successive batches.
The Worker has no DbContext or database connection and handles cancellation and temporary API failures.
commit: feat: process queued imports with the Worker
commit_steps: Implement Service login and API calls in the Worker.
Add the polling loop, cancellation and recovery from temporary failures.

title: Show authenticated live import progress
acceptance: /ws/import validates JWT, including browser access_token support.
ImportProgress with processed and total, and ImportCompleted, go only to the owning user's channel after persistence.
The browser displays progress, refreshes completed data and can recover status after reconnecting.
commit: feat: show import progress over WebSocket
commit_steps: Implement authenticated per-user WebSocket messages after persistence.
Connect the React progress view and reconnect handling.

title: Create monthly reports from the Worker schedule
acceptance: POST /api/reports/monthly produces the requested month's report with suitable role checks.
The Worker requests the previous month's report on the first day of the new month using a documented timezone.
Repeated scheduling or a Worker restart does not create duplicate reports for the same user and month.
commit: feat: schedule monthly budget reports
commit_steps: Add monthly report creation with duplicate protection.
Add the first-day schedule in the Worker.

title: Add expense distribution and history charts
acceptance: A chart shows expenses by category for the selected period.
A chart shows expense changes across months.
Labels, values and empty states agree with the API data.
commit: feat: add expense distribution and history charts
commit_steps: Build the expense-by-category chart.
Build the monthly expense history chart and empty states.

title: Add an explainable next-month expense forecast
acceptance: A simple documented method estimates next month's expenses from historical data.
The UI states the method and handles insufficient history.
Deterministic examples verify the calculation without implying financial certainty.
commit: feat: add next-month expense forecast
commit_steps: Implement and test a simple next-month forecasting method.
Show the forecast and explanation in React.

title: Build the MAUI client with MVVM
commit: feat: add the MAUI budget client
scope_note: Scope clarification from the student on 27 November 2026: a React website does not require a mobile application or a second client for grade 5.

title: Complete the required unit test coverage
acceptance: At least eight meaningful unit tests pass, including two using mocked dependencies.
Coverage includes calculations, category rules, validation or import behaviour as appropriate.
Tests are added alongside features and the README gives the test command.
commit: test: complete required budget service coverage
commit_steps: Complete missing unit tests for calculations, rules or imports.
Add the required mocked-dependency tests and record the test command.

title: Verify the complete application and fix integration issues
acceptance: A clean setup starts the API, React website and Worker using documented commands.
Checks include two users, malformed CSV, repeated processing, Worker restart and WebSocket reconnect.
Discovered defects have concrete fix commits and test results are recorded accurately.
commit: docs: record end-to-end verification results
commit_steps: Run the complete setup and integration checklist.
Fix each actual defect in its own relevant commit and record the final results.

title: Prepare the Estonian report and project demonstration
acceptance: The English README covers setup, configuration, roles, CSV format and all applications.
An Estonian report follows the supplied school guide and is exported to PDF.
The GitHub link, PDF and a short demonstration script are ready for submission.
commit: docs: add final report and demonstration guide
commit_steps: Finish the English setup README and demo instructions.
Write the Estonian report and export the school-formatted PDF.

title: Configure a shared PostgreSQL database
acceptance: A managed PostgreSQL database is available independently of either development PC.
Only the API uses the Npgsql EF Core provider and a private connection string.
The API connection can be configured on each PC and checked on the school network; credentials are not committed.
commit_steps: Add PostgreSQL provider and external connection configuration.
Document connection setup and verify connectivity.
commit: feat: configure shared PostgreSQL database

title: Document setup after the school PC is cleared
commit: docs: add school PC setup and recovery workflow
